title: Slot Efficiency Profiler and Adaptive Packager for Dedicated Pools
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Background: Dedicated fleets show skewed slot utilization across tenants and time-of-day bursts. Current heuristics map straight to slab sizes which leads to 12-28% idle GPU time on typical enterprise workloads or overcommit bursts that risk SLOs. This ticket builds a non-invasive profiler and an adaptive packaging engine to measure per-pool slot efficiencies and produce actionable pack suggestions for rightsizing and autoscaling policy tuning.

Goals:
- Produce a lightweight Slot Efficiency Profiler that runs as an agent on Dedicated pool control plane and emits per-pool metrics (p50/p90 occupancy, prefix-KV hit ratio, sustained QPS per slot, tail latency under varying batch sizes).
- Build an Adaptive Packager that takes profiler outputs + historical request traces to recommend: (a) slab sizes and shard counts, (b) autoscale policy parameters (scale-up threshold, cooldown, burst headroom), and (c) suggested request routing mixes to preserve throughput SLAs while reducing idle capacity.
- Surface recommendations in Console with exportable CSV and a one-click apply preview for patching pool configs.

Approach and design decisions:
- Profiler collects aggregated signals every 5m; sampling windows use moving 1h and 24h percentiles to avoid churn from short spikes.
- Use per-tenant 95th-percentile load to compute safe-downscale suggestions and 99th-percentile to validate SLO risk for scale-up triggers.
- Adaptive packager runs offline nightly and on-demand; it simulates packings using a cost model (GPU-hour unit cost + expected latency penalty) and ranks options by net unit-cost reduction while bounding SLO regression to <=2%.
- Start with conservative suggestions (max 30% reduction) for pools with recent high variance; aggressive suggestions allowed for stable low-variance pools.
- Ensure all recommendations are idempotent and reversible; include automatic rollback hooks if post-apply latency exceeds modeled expectations.

Acceptance criteria:
- Profiler agent deployed to staging pools and producing metrics to Grafana for at least 7 days.
- Adaptive Packager generates recommendations with a simulated cost delta and SLO risk estimate.
- Console UI shows recommendations with CSV export and an audit link.
- On a canary apply to two non-critical pools, we measure >=10% reduction in idle GPU time with <=2% change in p99 latency.

Metrics to track:
- Idle GPU time reduction (target >=10% across canary).
- Unit cost reduction per token (target >=8% for candidate pools).
- False-positive suggestion rate (target <5% revert by rollback).

Risks and mitigation:
- Risk: Underestimating tail traffic leads to SLO breaches. Mitigation: Conservative downscale bounds and 99th-percentile safety checks, plus rollback automation.
- Risk: Profiler overhead affects control plane. Mitigation: agent is low-frequency, compressed payloads, and sampling.

Rollout plan:
1) Spike & prototype (this ticket): profiler + offline packager + staging Console panel.
2) Canary: apply to 2 pools with scheduled rollback on anomaly.
3) Gradual ramp: 10% of pools after 2 weeks validation.
4) Full rollout with opt-in auto-apply option for low-risk customers.

Notes: This work intersects with autoscale economics (ENG-32677) and capacity-simulator (ENG-58209); coordination scheduled with those leads for model reuse.
